newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close higher on selective buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close higher on selective buying.

text.p: Thai stocks ended slightly higher on Wednesday on selective buying of some communication and bank stocks, brokers said.
The SET index closed 6.75 points higher at 700.62. The SET-50 index rose 0.72 points to 51.91. Turnover was 2.3 billion baht and advancers led decliners 164 to 128.
"Investors selectively bought some blue-chip communication and bank shares. But the market activity remained light," said one broker at Thai Financial Syndicate.
Brokers said many investors remained sidelined, awaiting the U.S. consumer price index which will be released later today.
"The market is waiting for the U.S. CPI data for a clearer picture of the U.S. interest rate trend," said another broker at SITCA Investment.
The market was apparently unaffected by the news of a loan default by One Holding, the investment arm of Finance One, because shares of both companies have been suspended, brokers said.
One Holding said it had defaulted on $13.50 million due as payment on its bills of exchange because of a liquidity problem.
The two tranches of B/E worth $1.0 and $12.5 million were due to be repaid on March 17 and 18 respectively, One Holding said in a filing to the Stock Exchange of Thailand.
In a separate filing, Finance One Plc said it was not affected by the inability of One Holding to meet repayment on bills of exchange.
Tipco Asphalt lost four baht to 104 on the most active trade of 93 million baht.
United Communication Industry rose three to 163. Bangkok Bank gained two to 181 and Thai Farmers Bank added one to 117. -- Anuchit Nguyen (662) 652-0642
